_head: Phase 1's measurements, replayable. Boxes are design pt on a 393x852 phone. The two references sit at DIFFERENT capture scales, because the recording's camera zooms in as the sheet opens: p1.png is 936x2029 at 2.381679 px/pt and p2.png is 1079x2339 at 2.745547 px/pt, and every probe carries its own "pt" so the command line's --pt is never what decides. p2's top 69.93pt is off the top of the video and is padded with the flat dimmed ground: no probe reads above y 70 on p2, and the delta table excludes that band. refkit batch applies one --pt to the reference and to the render alike, so the render has to be on the reference's own grid before it is probed: each row's "mine" names cap-<board>.png, which scratch/fit.py writes into scratch/mine beside refkit shoot's raw 3x output, at 936x2029 and 1079x2339 with the phone's 52pt corners masked the same way in both. Pointing --against at the raw shots instead reads every box at the wrong scale and errors a dozen probes. The twelve grid faces, the profile head and the two app icons are this repo's own art, not the source's, so no probe measures their ink: the probes near them read the white circle and the pale ground they sit in, which ARE measured. 'only: ink' is the mean of the darkest few percent, 'only: flat' the flat-neighbour census, 'only: all' the mode of a core-only crop. On a bbox, 'dark N' keeps pixels darker than N and 'bright N' keeps pixels lighter.
